title_original: Seth Rogen Says Brad Pitt and ‘12 Years a Slave’ Cast Would Visit ‘This Is the End’ Set to ‘Perk Up’ Because They Were ‘in a Bummed-Out Headspace’ While Filming

blocks.text: Seth Rogen and Brad Pitt spent time together while shooting very different films in 2013.

Rogen recalled Pitt, Michael Fassbender, Chiwetel Ejiofor and other cast members from “ 12 Years a Slave ” spending time on the set of his comedy “This Is the End” while the two films were both shooting in New Orleans. In a recent appearance on the “Happy Sad Confused” podcast, he spoke about his friendship with Fassbender, with whom he starred in 2015’s “Steve Jobs.”

blocks.text: “Actually, what’s so weird is I had met him — we made ‘This Is the End’ at the same time they made ’12 Years a Slave’ in New Orleans together,” Rogen told podcast host Josh Horowitz. “Understandably, the cast and crew of ’12 Years a Slave’ were in a bummed-out headspace a lot of the time.”

“12 Years a Slave” starred Ejiofor as a free Black man named Solomon Northup who was kidnapped in 1841 and sold into slavery in Louisiana. Fassbender played plantation owner Edwin Epps and Pitt played an abolitionist named Samuel Bass who helped Northup regain his freedom.

Meanwhile, Rogen was shooting “This Is the End” with Jay Baruchel, James Franco, Jonah Hill, Craig Robinson, Danny McBride and a host of other celebrities. The actors played dramatized versions of themselves in a bizarre apocalyptic scene at a Hollywood house party.

“So they would come and hang out on our set, and we would go to bars and stuff, and they would come hang out with us all the time, I think just because we were in a great mood all the time,” Rogen said. “We were having the time of our lives, and then you’d see Steve McQueen and Brad Pitt and Chiwetel would sulk in, and then we’d give them a few drinks and they’d kinda perk up.”

“12 Years a Slave” went on to win Best Picture and Best Adapted Screenplay (from Northup’s 1853 memoir “Twelve Years a Slave”) at the 2014 Academy Awards. Among its seven other nominations were acting nods for Ejiofor, Fassbender and Lupita Nyong’o.
